notes: Imposed on work performed in Denver (work-location basis, not residence). Employee OPT $5.75/month withheld by employer when compensation for services in Denver >= $500 in a calendar month. Employer pays separate Business OPT $4.00/month per taxable employee, and $4.00 per owner/partner/manager regardless of earnings; any entity active in Denver owes a minimum $4.00/month. Multiple employers: employee tax paid once (form TD 269). Employee working for one employer in several OPT jurisdictions pays only where most hours worked. Governmental/charitable entities exempt from Business OPT, not from withholding Employee OPT. Denver Revised Municipal Code Sec. 53-240 cited in guide; code text itself not fetched.

Official city page: OPT repealed effective Jan. 1, 2025; Dec 2024/Q4 2024 returns were the last, due 2025-01-31; city still accepts amended returns, prior-period returns and refund claims. Pre-repeal rule on the same page: $2 employee (withheld) + $2 employer match, gross earnings >= $250 per month, any work within city limits (work-location basis). Secondary corroboration that the repeal is in force and irreversible without a TABOR vote: Sentinel Colorado, 2025-12-08 https://sentinelcolorado.com/metro/contentious-head-tax-repeal-in-aurora-now-irreversible-city-officials-say/. Metro Denver EDC table (archived 2026-04-10) still lists Aurora at $2/$2/$250 = stale. Colorado State Controller policy (effective 2023-07-01) also lists Aurora = stale.

notes: City page: paid monthly by all employees who work within Glendale and earn more than $750 in a calendar month; $5 fee matched by employer = $10 total. Code 3.21.010(D): employee = person receiving >= $750 for a calendar month with any part of services performed within the city; 3.21.030: $5.00/month employee and $5.00/month employer for each employee working for a business located within Glendale (work-location basis, tied to a business located in the city); 3.21.050(B): money withheld from employee by employer held in trust for city. Owners/partners/proprietors owe the employer $5 even if under the $750 test. Same-employer multi-city rule: exempt if majority of hours in another city whose OPT was paid. Latest amendment cited in code: Ord. 2019-7.

City page: both portions $2/month ($4 combined), both apply when $250 or more is earned in a calendar month; employer reports and remits both portions (page does not use the word withhold; employer-collects wording is from Municode Art. 7 search snippet, Municode page blocked by Cloudflare). Owners/partners/officers earning < $250 owe only the employer portion. Tax instituted 1980-01-01; OPT license required for businesses located in the Village (one-time $10 fee); also needed for employers with employees working in the Village long term. Multi-city: payable to city where employee worked most; only primary employer withholds. Work-location basis (employee earns >= $250 for services in the city).

City page: $3/month per employee through payroll withholding, $3/month match from employer; employer remits both via MuniRevs; "a tax on employers and employees, not Sheridan residents" (work-location basis). The city page states NO wage threshold. Threshold $500 comes from secondary sources only: Metro Denver EDC table (archive 2026-04-10) and Boulder City Council information packet 2015-06-16 (https://documents.bouldercolorado.gov/WebLink/edoc/129158/2B%20%20Occupational%20Privilege%20Tax%20(OPT)%20aka%20Head%20Tax.pdf). Sheridan Code of Ordinances Ch. 62 Art. VI (Municode) was blocked by Cloudflare so code text not read. Another vendor guide reportedly lists $750 (unverified, not fetched).
